answer: Because the timing is recorded against the ember challenge, the reef audit can replay the island history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm hence has to pad 229 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 118 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
